title: mongo: include command name in Info column
description:
# Summary

Add MongoDB command name to `Info` column

# Background & Motivation

This is intended to help quickly see the command (e.g. `hello`, `ping`, `insert`, ...) sent to a MongoDB server.

Before:

![before](/uploads/dab8688897aff20e293d01eaa6306d85/before.png)

After:

![after](/uploads/9bb63bbc8eac0ff1fc9596b11dce2c4e/after.png)

Command names are read from `OP_QUERY` and `OP_MSG`. Though deprecated, modern drivers still use `OP_QUERY` for the initial command: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mongodb-wire-protocol/#opcodes:

> MongoDB 5.1 removes support for both `OP_QUERY` find operations and `OP_QUERY` commands. As an exception, `OP_QUERY` is still supported for running the [`hello`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/hello/#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.hello) and `isMaster` commands as part of the connection handshake.

When `OP_QUERY` is used to send commands (rather than legacy queries), the `admin.$cmd` collection is used.

The command name is expected to be the first field of a command document. Quoting the [OP_MSG specification](https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/message/OP_MSG.md):

> The command name MUST continue to be the first key of the command arguments in the `Payload Type 0` section.

## Testing

The screenshots above were generated with PyMongo:

```python
from pymongo import MongoClient

client = MongoClient("mongodb://localhost:27017/")
client["db"].command({"ping": 1})
```

The capture ([mongo-ping.pcapng](/uploads/e204eadf03834af7b6666aa58e46d3db/mongo-ping.pcapng)) includes an `ismaster` command sent over OP_QUERY and a `ping` command sent over `OP_MSG`.
